title: Croquetas de Jamon
subtitle: Crisp-fried croquettes with a creamy thick bechamel filling
excerpt: Golden fried croquettes with a rich, creamy filling made from a very thick bechamel spiked with onion and black pepper.
sourceNotes: A staple of Spanish tapas bars, croquetas are a labour of love that reward patience with a perfect crisp shell and molten centre.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the shaped, uncoated croquetas on a tray, then transfer to a bag. Fry from frozen, adding 2 extra minutes.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the quantity easily. The shaped croquetas freeze well for up to 3 months.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The bechamel must be made ahead and chilled for at least 2 hours, or overnight.

glossaryTerms.definition: A very stiff white sauce used as the filling for croquetas; much thicker than a standard bechamel.

content.text: This recipe makes about 16 croquetas and takes 1 hour of active cooking plus at least 2 hours of chilling time. The chilling is not optional: it is what allows the soft filling to firm up enough to shape and coat without collapsing in the frying oil.

The filling needs to be noticeably stiffer than a normal bechamel. Stir constantly over a low heat as it thickens so it does not catch on the base of the pan. When it pulls cleanly away from the sides and holds its shape when spread on a plate, it is ready. Spread it flat on a tray so it chills evenly and quickly.

items.prepNote: enough to fill the pan 4cm deep, for frying

content.text: Melt the butter in a medium saucepan over a medium heat. Add the chopped onion and soften for 5 minutes without colouring. Add the flour and stir vigorously for 2 minutes to cook out the raw taste.

Add the warm milk in a slow, steady stream, whisking constantly to prevent lumps. Switch to a wooden spoon and stir continuously over a low-medium heat for 10 to 12 minutes until the mixture is very thick, pulls away from the sides of the pan, and holds its shape.

Season very generously with black pepper. Spread the mixture onto a lightly oiled tray in an even layer about 2cm thick. Press a piece of cling film directly onto the surface to prevent a skin forming. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or overnight.

Set up three shallow bowls: one with plain flour, one with beaten egg, one with breadcrumbs. Scoop heaped tablespoons of the chilled filling and roll into cylinders about 6cm long. Dust in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs. Set on a clean tray.
Heat the vegetable oil in a deep frying pan to about 180C. Fry the croquetas in batches of 4 to 5 for 2 to 3 minutes, turning once, until deep golden and crisp all over. Do not overcrowd the pan.
Drain on kitchen paper and serve immediately while the centres are still molten and creamy.

items.problem: The croquetas burst open in the oil
items.solution: The filling was not chilled long enough or the oil was too hot. Chill for the full 2 hours and check the oil temperature with a thermometer before frying.
The milk was added too quickly. Always add it in a slow stream, whisking constantly, and lower the heat so you have time to work out any lumps.

items.problem: The coating falls off during frying
items.solution: Make sure each stage of the coating is applied thoroughly. Press the breadcrumbs firmly onto the surface and chill the coated croquetas for 15 minutes before frying.

content.text: Croquetas are found in every tapas bar in Spain and are considered a benchmark of a kitchen's skill. The secret is the quality of the

filling: it must be rich, well seasoned and silky inside the crisp shell. They take time and patience but freeze brilliantly, which makes a double batch practical. Once you have the technique, the filling variations are endless.
